rationale: This is essentially the archived Payout-Signed R&D Intensity with the switch made continuous and the expected sign reversed post hoc, and because both legs are demeaned the product is equally large for low-R&D/low-issuance firms, so the "premium to equity-funded R&D" story does not match what the expression actually ranks (and the positive sign fights the well-documented net-equity-issuance anomaly).

The debt-overhang-on-soft-assets mechanism applied to organic R&D is a defensible and reasonably distinct test from the gen-0 acquired-intangible version, though the double-demeaned product means the long leg also loads on low-R&D/low-debt-issuance firms, muddying the conditional interpretation.

A coherent stock-level asset-composition/capital-structure mismatch with a genuine coverage advantage over the gen-0 flow signals, but it is close to a mechanical product of two heavily studied characteristics (intangible intensity and leverage) and inherits the same four-quadrant sign ambiguity from centering both legs.

MIN is not the logical AND claimed: because DELTA(intan) is frequently negative while sstk/at is bounded below at zero, the signal collapses to intangible shrinkage/impairment for a large share of firms, so the bottom leg captures intangible write-downs rather than "no stock-financed expansion," and the two ratios have non-comparable scales.

Conditioning intangible intensity on the second moment of financing flows is a genuinely new angle in this archive, but the 5-year VOL on annual data will be noisy and coverage-thin, and the centered product again implies an unintended prediction for low-R&D/stable-financing firms.

A monotone [0,1] amplifier on share-issuance growth is largely a rediscovery of the well-known net share issuance anomaly rather than an identified interaction, and raw csho growth is contaminated by stock splits, which will dominate the extreme leg.
